title: Java State And Proxy Contracts Checkpoint

questions.prompt: A key’s equality fields mutate and a record wraps a shared mutable list. Which assumption is valid?

options.label: Require stable key equality and review the record’s nested ownership separately.
Record fields make the entire list deeply immutable.
A key can change equality safely because the same object remains.

questions.explanation: Stable equality is a map-key obligation. A final record field prevents replacing that field, not mutation of a referenced list; object identity alone does not repair changed key equality.

questions.prompt: Two workers read volatile count 4 before either writes its increment. What outcome is possible?

options.label: Volatile makes every multi-field transition one operation.
Both write 5; volatile does not make the increment atomic.

questions.explanation: Each increment includes a read, computation and write. Volatile ordering does not combine those steps, so the supplied interleaving can lose an increment without establishing a safe transition.

questions.prompt: A pooled thread handles two users through the same ThreadLocal. What cleanup is needed?

options.label: Removing on another unrelated thread clears every copy.
Remove request context on the owning thread, including exceptional exits.
The pool creates a new thread for every request.

questions.explanation: ThreadLocal holds per-thread state. Reused workers can carry earlier request context, and remove affects the current thread’s copy; cleanup must cover the owning request’s exit paths.

questions.prompt: A service invokes its own annotated method under default proxy-based transactions. What must be checked?

options.label: Self-invocation bypasses that proxy advice; inspect the actual intercepted entry.
The annotation guarantees a new transaction on every internal call.
All annotations are ignored even on external proxy calls.

questions.explanation: Default proxy advice operates at intercepted external entry. Self-invocation takes a different route; neither universal advice nor universal annotation failure describes both call paths.

questions.prompt: A checked exception escapes a transaction with default rules and no overrides. What is the default?

options.label: No exception can ever roll back.
Checked exceptions do not trigger rollback by default; explicit or global rules can change this.

questions.explanation: The documented defaults cover RuntimeException and Error. Checked exceptions need their applicable rule; global ALL_EXCEPTIONS and method-specific configuration must be inspected separately.
